problem_type: Canvas async writes must retain session and user-intent ownership
symptom: Undo restores an orphan running table; a pending table operation can mutate a restored project and regroup existing user nodes.
direct_cause: Fact progress uses user-edit barriers and projectId-only identity; optional batch landing lacks canvas generation checks and groups all selected nodes. Runtime updateNode also enters the unconditional document write boundary and could cancel an unrelated pending proposal.
class_root: Async completion and landing writes are not constrained by the originating canvas generation and operation-owned mutation set.
internal_only_reason: These are repository-owned journal and store invariants; Electron and model provider behavior does not determine ownership.
invariants: Runtime progress creates no user undo barriers.
A completion cannot write after canvas generation changes.
Batch landing groups only nodes created by that batch.
Async fact progress and results wait for any existing proposal to settle before reading and writing the latest table.
generality_proof: The fact write boundary and optional batch context cover full deconstruction, retry, and every materialization write; generation identity distinguishes even reopening the same project.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Await the existing canvas write boundary, validate generation, reread the current table, and persist runtime changes without user edit barriers.
Bind table landing writes to canvas generation and newly created nodes.
Send progress only to the trusted invoking renderer with its request and project identity; the receiver additionally enforces canvas generation.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Owns phase subscriptions and success/failure writes after IPC awaits.
Owns one-shot result merge after IPC await.
Calls materializeShotRow, which awaits defaults and model entries before shared create/update writes.
Progress carries requestId/projectId to the originating sender; factBridge binds that receipt to the originating canvas generation.

recurrence.reason: Every project switch, retry, and long model call can reach the same lifecycle boundary.
same_class_scan: rg writeTable and deconstruct in factBridge.ts verified full and retry calls.
rg applyCreate and syncShotNodeWithRow in storyboardRowActions.ts verified create and existing-node writes.

prevention.invariant: Async table writes retain canvas generation, runtime history policy, and operation-owned nodes.
prevention.failure_mode: Stale fact replies return without writing; stale batch materialization throws before create/update/confirmation.
prevention.strategy: Use existing undo-journal generation as identity, pass canWrite through existing gesture/capability boundary, and restrict grouping to the before/after created-node set. Fact progress, success, failure and retry converge on async writeTable, which awaits whenCanvasWriteBoundarySettled before rereading and mutation.

legacy_paths.rationale: The new table code is corrected in place; no parallel implementation or persisted legacy format is introduced.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Store/journal ownership is internal; no third-party version controls this invariant.

migration: No persisted schema change. Already-running snapshots still recover through the existing running-to-idle normalization.
residual_risks: Actual Electron journey and production confirmation remain part of root task verification.
